title: Flow friction mapping + open notes
content:
Context:
This doc captures a compact set of lab observations, quick wireframe notes, and a first-pass backlog grooming session after three moderated usability sessions focused on multi-route rollout flows (canary -> A/B -> full), cost visibility in token breakdowns, and streaming response controls. Sessions were semi-structured; participants were product platform engineers (2), a growth PM, and an infra-focused engineering manager (1). Goal: identify where users stall or guess and list micro-interventions (tiny UI/UX fixes) that reduce cognitive load without a major redesign.

Session summary (high level):
- Session length: ~45 minutes each. Tasks: 1) create a canary rollout for model v2, 2) verify cost impact of enabling KV cache for a route, 3) debug degraded tail latency and configure fallback.
- Main friction areas surfaced: unclear state after partial rollouts, token-cost details buried under multiple clicks, ambiguous streaming toggle semantics when using function/tool calls.
- Positive: participants appreciated per-route tracing link and quick preview of model outputs inside the route editor.

Raw participant quotes (verbatim-ish):
- "I created the canary but I wasn't sure if the traffic split actually applied — there was no obvious 'live' indicator."
- "Token cost is a nice metric but I have to open a separate panel and do manual math to see per-call cost with streaming on. Feels like two different worlds."
- "When fallback triggers, I want the console to show why — not just 'fallbacked to model X' — show the error and the fallback rule (region/capacity)."

Observed problems (mapped to microflow step):
1) Canary creation -> confirmation: no clear post-create state. User expectation: immediate visual confirmation on route list + timeline entry.
2) Cost inspection -> cross-panel mental model: users jump between route editor, cost explorer, and live traces. They want an embedded 'cost snapshot' at route settings.
3) Streaming controls -> inconsistent labels: "streaming: on" vs "enable streaming responses"; tool-calling flows make them unsure whether streaming will break structured tool output.
4) Fallback debugging -> opaque. The console shows the fallback model but not the trigger (quota vs latency vs error).

Low-effort wireframe ideas (sketch descriptions):
- A: "Canary ribbon" — small colored ribbon on active routes showing split (e.g., canary 5% orange, full green). Hover reveals a micro-timeline: created at, traffic %, last changed. Click => toast with link to rollout history.
- B: "Cost snapshot pill" — within route settings header, a small pill that shows avg tokens/call and estimated $/k calls. Clicking expands inline with toggle to view streaming-on vs streaming-off delta.
- C: "Fallback inspector panel" — contextual drawer that appears when a fallback event is selected from traces; top row shows trigger type (latency/quota/error) with a concise one-line cause and recommended action button (e.g., revert to previous model, increase concurrency limit).
- D: "Streaming info tooltip" — a short interaction microcopy that appears the first time a route uses function calls and streaming is enabled: "Streaming with function calls sends partial outputs; structured tool output is preserved — disable to receive final JSON only." Include a 'learn more' link.

Backlog grooming outcomes (prioritized quick wins):
P0 (next sprint):
- Add Canary ribbon + hover micro-timeline in route list (owner: Marcus). JIRA: CR-4127. Expected dev work: small UI piece + API to surface rollout history.
- Implement Cost snapshot pill (owner: Ruth). Low backend work: compute rolling avg tokens/call per route; UI toggle for streaming delta.

P1 (2 sprints):
- Fallback inspector panel (owner: Diego). Needs traces integration; stubbed # of trigger codes included.
- Standardize streaming labels and add first-time tooltip (owner: Product DEX team). Content + A/B test.

P2 (future):
- Add rollout timeline embedded in route details (larger effort across release-engineering and console).

Edge cases and open questions (for design review):
- How do we represent multi-factor fallbacks (e.g., latency + quota) succinctly in the inspector? Proposal: show primary trigger + secondary badges. But need SRE input on ordering.
- Privacy/permission: should cost snapshot be visible to non-billing users? We may need role-aware view. Action: check with security & compliance (ticket).
- Streaming + function call behavior: any change to streaming UI should sync with SDK docs and the streaming API docs. Action: link docs and coordinate release notes.

Quick usability notes (session-level micro-behaviors):
- Users often scan for color cues; absence of a persistent visual marker made them doubt changes had been applied.
- Toasts that disappear too quickly cause re-check behavior: participants tried to recreate actions to see the confirmation. Suggestion: persistent 'recent actions' panel reachable from header for last 5 route edits.
- Users expect a single canonical place for cost math. When asked, two of three said they prefer cost per-call (for quick estimates) and one preferred monthly projection. We'll present both in the pill with a toggle.

Design constraints and non-goals (decision log):
- Non-goal: full overhaul of route editor layout in this cycle — focus on micro-interventions.
- Constraint: changes must reuse existing rollout API; avoid new data models that require DB migrations for this quarter.

Next steps and owners:
- Marcus: prototype Canary ribbon in Figma and collect quick team feedback by 2026-04-26.
- Ruth: prototype cost pill and wireframe the streaming delta view; coordinate with billing for API requirements by 2026-04-30.
- Diego: spike on traces->fallback integration and mock payload examples for the inspector panel by 2026-05-06.
- Aisha (me): prepare a short 15-min demo for product sync; include videos of the three sessions and highlight the toast persistence issue.

Appendix: short session notes
- Participant A (platform eng): struggled with route naming collisions; used default auto-name and later couldn't find it in list. Suggested a 'recent edits' quick filter.
- Participant B (infra EM): wanted surface-level SLA impact estimates when toggling fallback policies.
- Participant C (growth PM): wanted a simple 'cost per 10k calls' estimate visible when evaluating rollout size.

End of notes — this is intentionally raw. Use for design/eng grooming and attach to CR-4127 as qualitative evidence.

Unresolved links to add to Confluence: recorded session clips (upload pending), raw transcripts, and the small Figma file Marcus will create.
